name: Mathematics (MS)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.notes:
University Coterminal Requirements
Coterminal master’s degree candidates are expected to complete all master’s degree requirements as described in this Bulletin. Coterminal Master’s Program describes university requirements for the coterminal master’s degree. Graduate Degrees describes university requirements for the master’s degree.
The university requires that the graduate advisor be assigned in the student’s first graduate quarter even though the undergraduate career may still be open. The university also requires that the Master’s Degree Program Proposal be completed by the student and approved by the department by the end of the student’s first graduate quarter.
Specific Departmental Requirements

• Candidates must complete an approved course program of 45 units of courses beyond the department requirements for the BS degree

• of which at least 36 units must be Mathematics Department courses.

• The Mathematics Department courses must be numbered 120 and above, and at least 18 units must be numbered between 200 and 297.

• Units from Math 360 do not count toward this degree.

• All coursework for the MS degree must be approved before the first quarter of enrollment in the program by the Director of Graduate Studies.

rules.name: 18 more units of Mathematics courses numbered 120 and above
Course program approved by the Director of Graduate Studies before the first quarter
3.0 GPA in Math courses and 3.0 in 200-level courses

gpa: The candidate must have a grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (B) in all coursework taken in Mathematics and a GPA of 3.0 (B) in the 200-level courses considered separately.
grading: 36 units of Mathematics Department courses must taken for a letter grade.
transferPolicy: Course transfers are not possible after the bachelor’s degree has been conferred.
reviewNotes: The audit checks 45 units of graduate coursework, at least 36 of them letter-graded Math courses numbered 120 and above (units from MATH 360 do not count toward the degree at all, and Math courses below 120 do not count), with at least 18 of those units numbered 200-297. Checked by hand: the Director of Graduate Studies approves your course program before your first quarter, and you need a 3.0 GPA in your Math courses and, separately, in your 200-level courses.
